Schedule bench run next Tue (Aisha/Evan + Diego)
action_items: Diego Martinez: run 1k request p50/p95 latency bench against their sample prompts - due 2028-03-22
Sophie Patel: send pilot contract draft and pricing matrix - due 2028-03-18

transcript:
Meeting started: 2028-03-15 16:00 UTC
Duration: 54 minutes
Attendees: Sophie (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Lena (Redwood Product), Tom (CTO), Aisha (Head of Data), Evan (ML Eng)

Summary: quick intro, product walkthrough focused on JSON mode structured outputs, console demonstration of schema binding, and Redwood Optimize recommendations for batching and quantization. Call ends with pilot/benchmark next steps and security packet request.

Topics: intro & goals; current infra; JSON mode / typed outputs overview; console demo: schema binding and fallbacks; Optimize: batching, KV caching, quantization profiles; deployment options and security; pilot scope and next steps.

00:00:07 Sophie: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm sophie from Redwood inference, i'm the account owner for northstar - quick round of intros, then diego will demo the json mode path, lena will show a couple console screens.
00:00:22 Tom: hey sophie, thanks, quick note we only have 55 minutes so maybe go heavy on the console screens and the optimize suggestions, we want to see how this reduces per token cost vs our current setup.
00:00:30 Sophie: totally. diego, over to you.
00:00:33 Diego: all right hi team, i'm diego, i'm an SE - i'll start with a short overview of JSON mode - think of it as "typed outputs" where you bind a schema to the model and the runtime enforces shape and fallbacks. i'll walk through a couple flows: successful typed response, schema mismatch fallback, and tool calling.
00:00:52 Aisha: quick Q - can we use our existing internal tools for augmentation or only Redwood tools?
00:00:57 Diego: you can wire external services via the tool calling layer, the console shows how to register HTTP and RPC hooks; the model will return the typed action and the runtime will invoke the tool. note: there is a small plug for the sandbox - we run the tool invocation in a controlled runner.
00:01:14 Evan: is that sandbox on our VPC or in the hosted environment? we have policy that any call to our internal APIs must originate from our VPC.
00:01:21 Lena: the private deployment option supports a console control plane with connectors in your VPC, so toolhooks can run from customer-hosted runners. we do a quick demo of the console connector later.
00:01:30 Diego: ok demo, sharing screen - 
00:01:40 (screen share glitch)
00:01:45 Diego: cool, so this is the console - runbook view - on the left is a schema library. here's an order-processing schema we use a lot, it's JSON Schema-ish but with typed enums and action shapes. you can pin a schema to a route.
00:02:06 Tom: sorry, are those "contracts" persistent across model versions? if we upgrade a model can the schema silently break behavior?
00:02:13 Diego: good question - schemas are versioned. the runtime can be configured with strict enforcement (reject responses that don't match) or permissive (attempt to coerce and log a regression). we also have automatic regression alerts tied to eval sets.
00:02:29 Aisha: what about fallback policies? we need graceful degradation - e.g., if the model can't produce the structured action, fall back to a simpler text response or a legacy service call.
00:02:36 Diego: yep, you can set per-route fallback chains: primary model -> cheaper quantized variant -> text-only fallback -> legacy service. the console shows the chain and the percentage traffic split for canaries.
00:02:51 Evan: any limit on number of schemas or tools registered? our app has 150+ microservices and many small action shapes.
00:02:58 Lena: no hard limit; large customers typically organize schemas in folders and use naming conventions. the console supports tagging and RBAC so only certain teams can edit.
00:03:12 Sophie: i'll quickly touch on Optimize - we ran some automatic suggestions for their example workload before this call. the tool looks at sequence length distribution and suggests batching windows, quantization profile (8-bit fp8-ish or int8), and prefix caching for common prompts.
00:03:28 Aisha: we use variable length prompts, lots of templates, and a median length of 120 tokens but tail to 1,200 on some analyst queries. how do you set the batching so latency stays low for interactive paths?
00:03:39 Diego: Optimize gives per-route recommendations. for routes with p50 < 150ms SLO we suggested a small microbatch (2-4) and aggressive prefix caching on shared prompts. for long batched jobs (async) we suggested batching up to 32.
00:03:55 Tom: can you show where that looks in the UI?
00:03:58 Diego: sure, switching to the Optimize page - you can see a histogram of seq length, the recommended quantization variant (we classified your model as a good candidate for q4_0 or int8 with per-channel scaling), and an estimated delta in tokens per second and per-token cost.
00:04:18 Evan: see that estimate numbers actually use our pricing? or is it generic?
00:04:22 Lena: estimates are configurable - for the hosted plan it uses Redwood's unit price; for Dedicated or Private you can input your infra cost or reserved GPU SKU to get an apples-to-apples estimate.
00:04:35 Aisha: security - we need to know how keys are managed when using private connectors, KMS?
00:04:41 Diego: Private deployments integrate with customer KMS/HSM. For hosted we support envelope encryption and our side can't see customer plaintext if you use client-side encryption. we'll send the security packet with SOC2 Type II and ISO artifacts.
00:04:54 Tom: what's the audit log retention? we need 12 months for certain endpoints.
00:04:58 Sophie: you can configure audit retention and export logs to your SIEM - the console supports push to S3 or a log forwarder. retention tiers are an add-on.
00:05:09 (crosstalk)
00:05:15 Diego: back to schema/tool calling - here's a sample: model returns { action: "getCustomer", params: { id: 123 }} - the runtime validates shape and then calls the registered tool. if the tool fails, we have retry/backoff and can optionally surface a structured error to the caller.
00:05:28 Evan: do you have RBAC on who can register tools? we can't have developers accidentally point to prod services.
00:05:33 Lena: yes, tools are managed entities with role-based access. plus connectors require signing and an allowlist of IPs or a private VPC tunnel.
00:05:44 Aisha: for a POC we want to run 1k concurrent small queries and measure p50/p95 and token cost. can you run against our sample prompts?
00:05:52 Diego: yes, we can run bench harnesses - typical approach: run in hosted first to validate latency then move to Dedicated or Private for final numbers. we'll instrument token breakdown and KV cache hit-rate.
00:06:04 Tom: curious about KV cache - i saw 'KV cash' in a doc once - does it hold user history? what about PII?
00:06:12 Diego: KV cache stores model key-value for autoregressive decoding (the attention cache), not user data. we also have prefix caching that caches full prompt prefixes - customers often scrub PII before caching or use short-lived encrypted caches in their VPC.
00:06:29 Sophie: small note - documentation sometimes says KV-cache or kvcache, transcription sometimes transcribes as 'KV cash' in our own notes, ha.
00:06:36 (laughter)
00:06:40 Diego: demo: tool calling flow, invoking a registered HTTP tool, shows logs - see the latency breakdown: tool invocation adds ~40ms but is batched when multiple calls share the same tool.
00:06:53 Aisha: is tool invocation synchronous only? some tools in our stack are async message queues.
00:06:58 Diego: we support async tool patterns - the model can emit an action that places a job on a queue and we return a structured acknowledge object; the runtime can later correlate the callback and emit an event.
00:07:10 Evan: we want to enforce schema on callbacks too.
00:07:12 Diego: callbacks have schema bindings as well - you can validate inbound callbacks and set guardrails.
00:07:20 Sophie: quick pivot to pricing models - for a 3-month pilot with reserved capacity we can offer a blended rate, we'll include Optimize savings estimates in the proposal.
00:07:31 Tom: what are the minimal support SLAs for pilot? we need 99.9 for p99 routing on the test cluster.
00:07:38 Sophie: pilot support includes SE hours for bench runs and a 1 business-day response SLA for critical issues. upgradeable to 24/7 for Dedicated.
00:07:47 (pause: screen transition)
00:07:55 Diego: showing console route editor - you can pin model version, attach schema, set fallback chain and routing policies (region, cost tier). also 'dry-run mode' lets you run traffic through typed-response validation without affecting production.
00:08:12 Aisha: dry-run mode sounds useful - will it count towards our quota?
00:08:16 Diego: dry-run can be configured to be non-billable for a short window; our suggestion is to use it for smoke tests.
00:08:24 Evan: latency accounting - will Optimize's suggestion change our p50 drastically? we saw tradeoffs in other vendors where batching improved throughput but hurt interactive median.
00:08:33 Diego: Optimize recommends microbatches with dynamic time windows: if no coalescing arrives in 12ms it will flush to keep latency tight. this gives most of the throughput upside but keeps p50 within bounds.
00:08:48 Tom: can the runtime auto-adjust based on real-time SLO violations?
00:08:52 Lena: yes, there's an autoscaling/autotune layer that adjusts batch windows and routes to different capacity tiers. policies are editable in the console.
00:09:03 Aisha: regarding quantization, you mentioned int8 - are there quality regressions we should expect? how are those surfaced?
00:09:09 Diego: Optimize runs evals on your prompt set with candidate quantized profiles and reports delta on key metrics: token-level edit distance, semantic similarity, and custom QA checks. you can set thresholds to block automatic fallback to a quantized variant.
00:09:25 Evan: oh nice - can we bring our own eval harness or do we have to use Redwood's?
00:09:29 Lena: you can upload your eval harness or link to a Git repo; the console will run the jobs in a sandbox.
00:09:36 Tom: security again - SSO/SAML on the console?
00:09:40 Sophie: yes SSO/SAML + SCIM for provisioning, and fine-grained RBAC. we'll include a sample SAML metadata file in the packet.
00:09:49 (someone briefly muted)
00:09:55 Diego: quick demo of an intentional schema mismatch - model emits extra fields, runtime logs an alert and sends the event to the regression stream. you can configure Slack or webhook notifications.
00:10:09 Aisha: great, that's our main concern - we can't have silent regressions after model upgrades.
00:10:14 Diego: agreed - the default is to fail-fast on strict routes and send the sample to a review queue with a diff view.
00:10:22 Sophie: let's talk pilot scope - we propose: 6 routes (2 interactive lead gen, 2 async batch enrichment, 2 tool-calling workflows), 3-week bench and 8-week pilot, cloud or private depending on final security review.
00:10:36 Tom: timeline looks okay but we need legal and procurement alignment before committing. can you send a starter SOW and T&Cs?
00:10:44 Sophie: yes i'll include a template SOW and the pricing tiers.
00:10:48 Evan: bench specifics - we'll provide a 10k prompt corpus with typical and edge cases. we want p50, p95, cost/token, cache hit rate.
00:10:57 Diego: perfect - please also include example state keys for prefix caching to get realistic hit rates.
00:11:05 Aisha: data residency - some of our EU customers require data to stay in eu-west-1. can routing be region-aware?
00:11:11 Lena: yes, routing policies allow region pins and data locality constraints. for private deployments we can ensure everything stays in your region.
00:11:20 Tom: any limitations with long-running contexts? we have threads up to 50k tokens for some analytics.
00:11:26 Diego: our runtime supports segmented contexts and offloading KV to disk for large contexts; however long-context workflows often require Dedicated or Private with higher memory GPUs. Optimize will flag those routes.
00:11:41 (short silence)
00:11:52 Sophie: ok wrapping up demo - diego, do you want to call out any gotchas?
00:11:57 Diego: watch out for tool auth - we recommend short-lived tokens and connector tunnels for anything hitting internal APIs. also when using prefix caching scrubbing is important to avoid storing PII.
00:12:08 Tom: noted. one last question - how do you handle cost attribution so product teams see token spend per route?
00:12:15 Lena: console has per-route cost and token breakdown by user, token type (prompt/completion/embedding), and model variant. we also export to billing reports for chargebacks.
00:12:28 Aisha: ok that's helpful.
00:12:32 Sophie: let's summarize actions - diego will run bench, sophie will send contract, aisha will share prompts. any other asks?
00:12:40 Tom: please include security contact and SOC2 docs in the packet.
00:12:43 Sophie: yes.
00:12:45 (meeting moves into Q&A and peripheral questions)
00:13:05 Evan: question about model catalogs - do you host open models only or do customers bring their own?
00:13:10 Diego: both - we curate open models and maintain performance profiles; customers can bring their own model artifacts for Private or Dedicated. when bringing your own we help with kernel selection and quantization.
00:13:23 Aisha: do you support on-prem air-gapped installs?
00:13:25 Lena: yes, air-gapped on-prem package with an ops bundle; we usually do a short engagement to help with instantiation and KMS integration.
00:13:34 Tom: procurement will ask about indemnity and data processing -- legal will be in touch.
00:13:39 Sophie: understood.
00:13:42 (longer demo follow-ups, 20 minute mark they switch to pricing)
00:33:50 Sophie: pricing overview - hosted per-token, dedicated monthly commitment, private license + support. discounts for reserved capacity pilots.
00:34:02 Tom: can you ship a SKU that maps to our finance system?
00:34:06 Sophie: yes, we'll include a line-itemed quote and SKU mapping.
00:34:15 (closing)
00:34:23 Sophie: thanks everyone - recap and next steps: we'll share security packet and pilot SOW, diego will schedule bench with aisha/evan next week, sophie will send pricing and starter SOW.
00:34:36 Tom: thanks, good session.
00:34:40 (meeting ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-recognitions (KV cash -> KV cache), speaker labels sometimes generic. There were a couple screen glitches.
